Choose your sleeve color and team identity

Compare white, blue, purple and brown for rank-inspired design development, plus black and olive for custom team collections. Final competition suitability depends on the event requirements and the approved garment.

White · Blue · Purple · Brown · Olive · Black shown in overview

Plan the fit, seams and branding together

Raglan long sleeve pattern

Specify sleeve length, upper-arm fit, underarm ease and torso coverage together. Check reaching, framing and grappling movements on the worn sample.

Flatlock seam development

Use the four-needle / six-thread flatlock direction in your brief, then approve the actual stitch configuration and inside finish. Review collar, raglan, side-body, cuff and hem seams for comfort and workmanship.

Private-label logo layout

Plan chest, back and sleeve branding with panel seams and stretch in mind. Select sublimation, transfer or screen-print decoration according to the fabric and artwork, then approve color and application on the sample.

Confirm stretch, recovery, opacity, drying performance and abrasion requirements against the selected material and agreed tests.

Rank-inspired colors and competition requirements

For a ranked BJJ rash guard project, provide the event, year, belt and age division before artwork approval. Color names alone do not establish compliance. Olive is a custom academy or team color, not a belt rank.

IBJJF has published a 2027 update with separate white- and black-belt color rules and visibility requirements for colored ranks. For example, its 2027 white-belt guide calls for a predominantly white shirt; the black-body / white-sleeve concept shown here should not be treated as automatic approval.

IBJJF uniform information · IBJJF 2027 No-Gi uniform guide. Confirm the rules that apply to your event before production.

Custom long sleeve BJJ rash guard: buyer questions

Can we customize long sleeve rash guards with our academy logo?

Yes. Submit authorized chest, back and sleeve artwork, preferred colors, labels and packaging requirements. TONTON reviews the decoration method and placement with the selected fabric before sample approval.

Are all displayed colors approved for ranked No-Gi competition?

No blanket competition approval is claimed. The images are colorway design references. Check the current rules for the event, belt and age division, including color coverage and front/back visibility. Olive is a custom team color rather than a belt-rank designation.

What fabric composition and GSM does this rash guard use?

Choose and confirm the compression-knit swatch, composition, weight, stretch recovery and opacity in the project specification. Exact percentages and GSM for this reference are confirmed during quotation and sampling.

How are the seams, collar and cuffs specified?

The development brief calls for raglan long sleeves, flatlock seam construction and elastic cuff and hem finishing. Confirm the stitch configuration, seam comfort, sleeve length and body coverage on a physical sample.

What are the MOQ and sample lead time?

Selected TONTON projects start from 10 pieces. Confirm the applicable minimum by style, design, color and size allocation. The selected-project sample target is 3–7 days after usable artwork and product details are confirmed; request a project-specific schedule.

Can we order several sleeve colors as one product program?

Yes, discuss the white, blue, purple, brown, black and olive color directions as one product development program. Send quantities by color and size so the team can confirm material availability, minimums and the quotation.

Are these images and video photographs of a finished sample?

The supplied visuals are product design presentations with placeholder CUSTOM LOGO artwork. The video is generated. Use a physical sample and the approved specification to confirm the final fabric, seams, fit and branding.
